issues.legal_issue: An unexplained and prejudicial delay in initiating disciplinary proceedings can justify quashing the charge memo.
material_facts: The alleged irregularity concerned a sale deed issued in 1990, but the charge memo was issued in 2000.
The relevant records were available to the Board, and it had taken no action for about ten years; the Board gave no convincing explanation for the delay.

The Board said the irregularity came to light in an audit report for 1994–1995, but the Court found that explanation unconvincing in light of the statutory requirements for annual accounts and audits.
The employee had retired, and continuing the proceedings would cause substantial prejudice and mental anguish.
issues.conclusion: The charge memo was quashed because continuing the disciplinary proceedings after the unexplained delay would be prejudicial; the employee was entitled to retiral benefits in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: There is no predetermined rule that delay always requires termination of disciplinary proceedings. The court must assess the case’s facts, including the nature and complexity of the charge, the cause of delay, prejudice to the employee, and whether the employee caused the delay or the employer properly explained it. Unexplained abnormal delay may make proceedings unfair. The Court relied on State of Madhya Pradesh v. Bani Singh, which upheld quashing proceedings after an unexplained delay, and State of A.P. v. N. Radhakrishan, which requires balancing the relevant factors. Sections 118 and 119 of the Tamil Nadu State Housing Board Act, 1961 require annual submission of account abstracts and annual audit, and undermined the Board’s explanation that the irregularity surfaced only through a later audit report.

rule.if: disciplinary_charge_proceeding and substantial_initiation_delay and no_convincing_delay_explanation and (employee_prejudiced_by_continuance or prolonged_serious_integrity_charges)

predicates.disciplinary_charge_proceeding: The employer initiated a disciplinary proceeding by issuing a charge memo to an employee.
predicates.substantial_initiation_delay: The employer waited a substantial time after the alleged conduct before initiating the disciplinary proceeding.
predicates.no_convincing_delay_explanation: The employer did not provide a convincing explanation for the delay in initiating the proceeding.
predicates.employee_prejudiced_by_continuance: Continuing the proceeding would substantially prejudice the employee, including through prolonged mental anguish.
predicates.prolonged_serious_integrity_charges: The employee remained under prolonged charges concerning serious misconduct or integrity.

issues.definition: When an employer initiates a disciplinary proceeding after a substantial delay without a convincing explanation, and continuance would prejudice the employee or prolong serious integrity charges, the charge memo is quashed.
